subject: Private deployment acceptance kickoff — networking, KMS, and evidence Q&A
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Crisp <lauren.crisp@acmehealth.com>; NetworkOps Team <netops@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:15:00 +0000
Subject: Private deployment acceptance kickoff — networking, KMS, and evidence Q&A

Hi Lauren / NetworkOps,

Thanks again for choosing Redwood for the private deployment. Before we schedule the operational kick-off, I wanted to consolidate a short acceptance checklist and a couple of specific questions so we can avoid back-and-forth during the handoff. I attached a one-page checklist (redwood-private-onboard-checklist-v1.xlsx) and a short KMS options summary (kms-integration-options.pdf).

Top asks from our side:
- Confirm VPC peering/private interconnect window (proposed: 2027-04-12 02:00–04:00 UTC). Will that maintenance window work?
- KMS: do you prefer customer-managed keys in Cloud KMS or an on-prem HSM? If HSM, what vendor/connector do we need to support (YubiHSM, Thales)?
- Routing: will outbound egress be SNAT through a single NAT gateway, or will you allow our service subnet direct egress? We need an allowlist for egress IPs if you SNAT.
- Evidence: your security team asked for examples of audit logs and token-level access logs. We can share a redacted sample if that helps.

If we can get answers to the above, we’ll run the preflight smoke tests and handover playbook in the next sprint. Proposed next steps:
1) Lauren confirms the maintenance window and KMS preference.
2) NetworkOps shares the CIDR for peering and the egress plan.
3) We schedule a 60-min kickoff with infra and security (I’ll invite Neha and Alex).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite after I hear from you.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: redwood-private-onboard-checklist-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), kms-integration-options.pdf (doc)
From: Lauren Crisp <lauren.crisp@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: NetworkOps Team <netops@acmehealth.com>; security@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 13:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deployment acceptance kickoff — networking, KMS, and evidence Q&A

Ben — thanks for the clear list. A few quick answers: 

- Maintenance window: 2027-04-12 02:00–04:00 UTC is fine for us. Please keep the change window under 2 hours.
- KMS: we prefer our on-prem HSM for key management. We currently use a Thales Luna HSM appliance. We'll need you to support PKCS#11 integration; our security team can share connector details.
- Egress: we will SNAT outbound traffic through a single egress IP (we'll provide the IPs next week).
- Audit evidence: yes please send a redacted sample of audit and token access logs — security will need an example to validate retention and redaction practices.

Also attaching a short intake form from our security team — they ask that any third party provide how long logs are retained and whether token metadata is redacted by default.

Lauren Crisp
Director, Cloud Operations | Acme Health
lauren.crisp@acmehealth.com | +1 (617) 555-2134

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Crisp <lauren.crisp@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 18:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deployment acceptance kickoff — networking, KMS, and evidence Q&A

Thanks Lauren — helpful. Notes from infra/security for the kickoff agenda: 

- KMS/HSM: we support PKCS#11 for Thales Luna; Alex will validate the connector and confirm whether we need a customer-side proxy. Action: Alex to validate Thales firmware compatibility (target 2027-04-06).
- Audit logs: standard retention is 90 days in the hosted view; for Private we can configure retention per contract. Need to confirm retention SLA in contract addendum. Action: I’ll loop Legal for a short clause.
- Egress IPs: please send the exact SNAT IPs and the ASN if you peer via a cloud provider. We will produce an allowlist and include it in the runbook.
- Peering prep: we require the peer CIDR and a named point-of-contact for the maintenance window (for rollback).

Also, small ask — do you have a sample of the token-level access log with metadata redacted? If not, Ben — can you produce a redacted sample for their security team to review? Use synthetic IDs and remove any PII.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Infrastructure Security | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0477
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Crisp <lauren.crisp@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deployment acceptance kickoff — networking, KMS, and evidence Q&A

Lauren — great, thanks for the quick reply and the intake form.

Planned deliverables prior to the kickoff (I’ll attach these to the HubSpot deal):
- Redacted audit & token access sample (PDF) — target 2027-04-05 (Ben)
- Connector compatibility note for Thales Luna (Alex) — target 2027-04-06
- SNAT IP allowlist + ASN (Acme) — please send by 2027-04-07 so we can add to the runbook
- Updated acceptance checklist with retention SLA draft for Legal (Neha / Marissa) — target 2027-04-08

I’ll schedule the kickoff for 2027-04-09 16:00 UTC (60 mins). If that doesn’t work, tell me preferred times and we’ll adjust.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to getting this into staging.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redacted-audit-sample.pdf (to be delivered)
